meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be direct: why does my son have a zero, and why did he find out from his phone in the middle of class?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down. What else do you have, Hale, besides the checker?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

One line you say "isn't anywhere in Hamlet." Students misquote, Hale, and a misquote doesn't get a zero under your own procedure. Show me where it sits in the essay, and then tell me what else you have.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
"It seems to run in the family." You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. I'm writing that down, and the principal will hear it from me today.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn from Owen's mark and a proper apology, and I will be speaking to the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and an apology, and she is taking it to the principal.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" earned a flat okay and a small sign of ground, because you owned it in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" cost the most, because bringing up Claire made her go cold and put the principal back on the table.
Try next time: after owning the zero, put one dated document tied to Owen's own work in front of her, such as his process or other samples of his writing, instead of a single line she can dismiss as a misquote.
